messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty PD-ENG-SRE page fired for metrics.pipeline: scrape_proxy_exporter failures (threshold breached) + logs.ingest.consumer_lag > 10k. Auto-escalation to on-call (olivia).

olivia: ack @incident-bot - I'm on it. @mateo can you standby for logs + consumer checks?

mateo: on it. pulling exporter logs from scrape-proxy pod. running:
```bash
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/scrape-proxy --tail=200\```

mateo: log excerpt: 
```
2026-03-15T12:07:01Z WARN upstream_request failed status=502 host=upstream-cluster/metrics-endpoint latency=1500ms
2026-03-15T12:07:03Z ERROR timeout reading response from upstream host=metrics-backend timeout=2s
2026-03-15T12:07:04Z WARN request_rate spike=2.4x concurrent=120
```

olivia: looks like upstream timeouts + traffic spike. scrape-proxy hitting 2s timeouts and 502s. quick mitigation: restart scrape-proxy pods to clear stuck connections and then increase timeout. initiating rollout restart: `kubectl -n infra rollout restart deploy/scrape-proxy`

deploy-bot: rollout started for deploy/scrape-proxy (namespace: infra). image unchanged; rolling restart.

mateo: after restart, quick health check: `curl -sS http://scrape-proxy.infra:9100/metrics | head -n 5` returns metrics. but prometheus scrape_errors still high for ~2 minutes.

olivia: scrapes recovering for most targets, but we still see heavy consumer lag on logs-ingest: checking kafka consumer group:
```bash
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka:9092 --describe --group metrics-logs-consumer
TOPIC\tPARTITION\tCURRENT-OFFSET\tLOG-END-OFFSET\tLAG\tCONSUMER-ID
logs_raw\t0\t1023456\t1038000\t14544\tconsumer-1
logs_raw\t1\t1023001\t1037999\t14998\tconsumer-2
```

priya: that lag is dangerous. autoscale hasn't kicked in because HPA target is CPU-based and consumers are IO-bound. scaling metrics-consumer deployment from 3 -> 6 replicas now: `kubectl -n ingest scale deploy/metrics-consumer --replicas=6`

deploy-bot: scaled deploy/metrics-consumer to 6 replicas.

mateo: new consumers started, rebalancing partitions. monitoring offsets...

olivia: observed metric: `consumer_lag{topic="logs_raw"}` dropping: 14544 -> 6200 -> 320 -> 40 within ~10 minutes. good.

mike-customer-ops: pinged impacted customers (acme-inc, glidepay) at 12:13 with templated message: "We're investigating missing metrics and delayed logs ingestion; dashboards may be stale. We'll share ETA shortly."

olivia: customer impact summary: dashboards and alerts depending on fresh metrics/logs were delayed for ~14 minutes window (12:07-12:21). no evidence of data loss — backlog replayed. severity classified Sev2.

priya: root cause hypothesis: scrape-proxy upstream timeouts caused throttling which spiked downstream buffering and increased write pressure to Kafka, which pushed consumer lag above autoscale trigger. Follow-ups:
- increase scrape-proxy upstream timeout from 2s -> 5s (pr to infra repo)
- add circuit breaker on high error-rate to shed non-critical scrapes
- change HPA to include custom metric (consumer_lag or queue depth) for ingest consumers
- run a capacity test for scrape-proxy during peak shard sizes

olivia: immediate actions and owners:
- mateo -> postmortem draft + patch for scrape-proxy timeout + config validation tests (ETA: EOD)
- priya -> HPA + autoscale tuning + runbook update (ETA: 48h)
- olivia -> customer comms thread + severity notes + update PD incident to resolved when stable (ETA: +30m)

mateo: creating follow-up GitHub issues now. noted need for a unit test covering high-latency upstream.

olivia: updating PagerDuty: marking incident as "resolved" in PD console, leaving note about mitigation (restart + scale) and customer impact.

incident-bot: PD-ENG-SRE incident resolved (auto-note: responders acknowledged: olivia, mateo).

olivia: thanks team. leaving this thread open for any additional telemetry anomalies. will file postmortem and link here. :white_check_mark:
